clue.text: Conrad is surprisingly bitter

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a man named Conrad has unexpectedly turned resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges CONRAD and IS together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic humour is grimly mocking and cynical, a sense close to bitter.

clue.text: Wash and brush up

explanation.surface: An instruction to freshen yourself up before going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash' is to scour clean; 'brush' is low scrubby vegetation, the second sense. 'up' just tucks the surface into the phrase brush up.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash hard is to scour, and brush is undergrowth, scrubland of small bushes.

clue.text: Flirting daughter joins union

parts.note: an alliance is a union of parties or nations

explanation.surface: A father frets that his daughter is getting into a flirtatious relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is light amorous play, casual romance without commitment.

clue.text: Ann turned out to be enthusiastic for material

indicators.note: turned out signals the three letters of the name Ann being arranged differently

parts.note: keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Ann proves surprisingly eager about some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ann' in the surface looks like a person, but her name is only letters; 'turned out' signals that they are rearranged. Nankeen is named after Nanjing, where the cloth was first made.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Trust mischievous act to be a swindle

parts.note: confidence is trust placed in someone
a trick is a prank or mischievous act

explanation.surface: Betraying someone's trust in a playful way turns out to be fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A con game in which a fraudster first wins the victim's trust, then cheats them.

clue.text: Drink coming afterwards

explanation.surface: A barman describes a drink served after another.
explanation.walkthrough: A chaser is a drink taken after a spirit; one who chases comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: A short drink downed after another, and a pursuer who follows behind.

clue.text: Ruminants on edge in the field

parts.note: cows are cud-chewing animals, ruminants
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: Cattle grazing at the margin of a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a flower found growing in meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow wild primula of English meadows and pastures.

clue.text: Particularly mention condition of London district before agent went round

indicators.note: went round shows the agent enclosing the other letters

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: before sets the district's letters ahead of the condition

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London, East Central
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Someone details an agent's circuit of a London district and its terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To specify is to name or state something precisely and in detail.

clue.text: Again letting, letting go

explanation.surface: A landlord renting a flat out again, and freeing a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-LEASING it means letting out once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasing anew is renting again; releasing is setting free.

clue.text: Sleeve made from rag by the local area network

explanation.surface: A garment's arm stitched from cloth scraps next to some computer cabling.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan sleeve runs in one piece up to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: Film modern southern dance

parts.note: new means modern
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A recent movie about a dance from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel is a short cinema film of current events.

clue.text: Be right alongside one repeatedly having complaint

indicators.note: repeatedly means the whole assembled group of letters appears twice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being correct alongside someone who keeps grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by lack of vitamin B1, an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Old leather corslet — made by coral — I included

indicators.note: included shows the letter I being put inside the reworked letters
made by suggests the letters of coral are refashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A piece of ancient armour apparently crafted from coral, with something extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' rearranges CORAL to LORCA, and 'included' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorica was a Roman cuirass or breastplate, originally of leather.

clue.text: Rule I leave the big guns

indicators.note: leave means the letter I departs from the word for a rule

parts.note: an ordinance is a decree or rule

explanation.surface: A ruler declares that they are walking away from the heavy weaponry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery, heavy guns and military supplies.

clue.text: Unburdened oneself on holiday, extremely rich

parts.note: off means away from work, on holiday
loaded is slang for very wealthy

explanation.surface: A wealthy person on vacation sheds their worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Offloaded means got rid of a burden, often by telling others one's troubles.

clue.text: Pulp, before year one, ancient scrolls

parts.note: pap is soft pulpy food
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Old manuscripts are pulped before the year begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyri are documents written on papyrus, rolls from ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Spanish for dog shark

parts.note: por is a Spanish word for for
a beagle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a Spanish word for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a large mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Smallest number of sheep in the distance

indicators.note: in places the sheep within the distance letters

parts.note: FT, feet, is a measure of distance
ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Only a handful of sheep can be seen far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the distance' reads as far away, but 'in' is the container signal and 'distance' gives the abbreviation for feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewest is the least in count, the lowest quantity.

clue.text: Buzzer is heard initially to be easily irritated

parts.note: a wasp is an insect that buzzes

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An insect's droning is irritating from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish describes someone sharp-tempered and quick to snap.

clue.text: Twisting in roots showing malformation

indicators.note: showing malformation means the letters of in roots are deformed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Contorted growth in a plant's roots signals deformity.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting, a strain from rotation.

clue.text: Insuring for travelling a distance

explanation.surface: An insurance policy for a journey of some length.
explanation.walkthrough: Covering a risk is insuring it; covering ground is travelling over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover is to insure against loss, and to cover miles is to journey that far.

clue.text: Louvre's remarkable woven fabric

indicators.note: remarkable hints that the letters of Louvre's are reworked strikingly

explanation.surface: A Paris museum's striking tapestry collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges LOUVRES, keeping the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Velours is a velvety cloth with a soft pile.

clue.text: One taken from bed to table

definitions.text: One taken from bed to table

parts.words: One taken from bed to table
parts.note: the bed is not for sleeping but a seabed shellfish bed, its occupant carried off to be served at dinner

explanation.surface: Someone is carried from their bed straight to the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish is harvested from beds in the sea and served raw at the table.

clue.text: Spoke boldly and said it more loudly

explanation.surface: Someone spoke out confidently and raised their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: To talk up is to promote boldly, or literally to speak louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Talked up means promoted with confident praise, and also spoke at a higher volume.

clue.text: Plate — it was removed from patient

indicators.note: was removed from means the two letters it come out of the following word

explanation.surface: A dish was taken away from a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was removed from' takes IT out of PATIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is a shallow dish holding the bread at Communion.

clue.text: Welshman has most of the paper and single drink

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the paper word is dropped

parts.note: a quire is a set of sheets of paper
I, the Roman one, means single

explanation.surface: A Welshman has nearly all the newspaper and one cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the E of QUIRE (24 or 25 sheets of paper).
explanation.definitionFit: A daiquiri is a rum cocktail with lime juice.

clue.text: Old city chap requiring immediate attention

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia
a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A man from an ancient city needs prompt help.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing must be dealt with at once.

clue.text: Prune from inside hornets' nest

annotationWithheld.why: Prune from inside hornets' nest (6): DEHORN can only be DEN round HOR, but nothing in the clue as held signals taking just HOR from hornets; the clue looks garbled and no search found the original

clue.text: One man trapped another in old district of Lincolnshire

indicators.note: trapped shows the first man's name holding the second man inside

parts.note: Ken is a man's name
Steve is another man's name

explanation.surface: One man has caught another in an old English county region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' signals one name enclosing the other. Lincolnshire is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Kesteven was one of the three historic administrative parts of Lincolnshire.
